criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`. A test with simulated low space (ATHENA_FREE_BYTES) after the build shows the job ends held, not Failed, with no `athena retry`, no verifier or producer verdict recorded, and outcome text naming `environment: low disk` with free and required amounts. It fails on pre-change code.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: 129 passed, 0 failed. Two new tests cover this. `low_disk_after_the_build_holds_the_job_and_does_not_fail_it` runs a real drain and asserts: failed_item None; outcome `environment: low disk`; the text names 3.0 GB and 10.0 GB; the job is Dispatched with no outcome, score or verification; no Verifier invocation; no `athena retry` text; the hold marker carries the amounts. `low_disk_after_the_checks_holds_the_job_before_the_verifier_runs` covers the verifier gate. On the base, go returned Finished(Failed) with an `athena retry` reason, so these Dispatched/no-outcome assertions would fail. That last point comes from reading the base code and the replaced assertions; I did not run the tests on the base.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`. A test shows a later drain pass, after simulated free space is raised, resumes the held job from its kept candidate with no new producer run and no `athena retry`, and the job finishes.
criteria.evidence: `a_later_pass_resumes_the_held_job_from_its_kept_candidate` passed. Pass 2 lands (landed 1, outcome passed) as one new job whose request is `try again on <A>`. It made exactly one more reader call and no extra planner or producer call. Output has `resume     job <A> kept its candidate`, and A's hold marker is cleared. The test never runs the `athena retry` command.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`. A test shows space that stays short across passes leaves the job held and uses no drain attempt.
criteria.evidence: `space_that_stays_short_leaves_the_job_held_and_uses_no_attempt` passed. Every pass has failed_item None and a stop that is not RepeatedFailure. Pass 2 makes one new job, held at dispatch with the amounts. Pass 3 makes no new job. The planner, producer and verifier counts stay at (0,1,0), and nothing lands.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. Tests show a low-disk hold before the checks and before the verifier is not counted as a work failure in introspection, failure classes or the scope guard. The updated scope_guard test a_low_disk_job_is_read_as_an_environment_attempt passes by asserting go returns the LowDisk hold with no attempt recorded and the later resume lands as resumed. Idle-build cleanup still runs first, and removes only Athena-owned finished-job directories.
criteria.evidence: The full `cargo test -p athena-core` run exited 0. The filtered runs also passed: low_disk (5 tests), scope_guard (26), disk:: (23). The rewritten scope_guard test asserts: go returns an error that downcasts to LowDisk; there is no outcome; attempts is empty; no pause or flag file. After freeing space, retry plus go lands, with attempts[0].resumed true and verdict Accepted. Two run/tests.rs tests assert no introspection records. They also show the line `disk       removed build directory of job` comes before `held`. The idle job's target/ is removed, while its work/ source, a non-job `jobs/scratch/target` and a directory outside jobs/ are kept. Failure classes are derived from introspection records, which a hold does not write.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test binary`. `athena status` shows the held job with its low-disk reason and the amounts.
criteria.evidence: The new test `status_shows_a_job_held_for_low_disk_with_the_amounts_and_that_the_next_drain_resumes_it` passed. It spawns the real binary's `athena status`. The line shows `interrupted`, `environment: low disk: 3.0 GB free, 10.0 GB required` and `the next drain resumes it`, and the JSON hold field matches. The full binary suite is covered by the recorded `cargo test --locked`.

findings.summary: A comment in the rewritten scope_guard test says the held job 'closes with no outcome'; a held job does not close, it stays dispatched.
findings.evidence: The comment reads 'the job closes with no outcome', while hold_for_disk leaves the job Dispatched.

findings.summary: While space stays short, the next drain pass still runs a reader call to make a retry job, which is then held at dispatch. This costs one reading per held job.
findings.evidence: interrupted_work lists any dispatched job with no process, whatever the free space. Pass 2 of space_that_stays_short... makes job B with one reader call. It is bounded (pass 3 adds nothing). Checking free space before retrying a disk-held job would avoid the call.

findings.summary: The D146 figure '10 cases in 9 jobs' comes from records/, which are absent in this snapshot, so I could not check it.

summary: The candidate keeps the hold-and-auto-resume design and fixes both earlier findings. Low disk at the gate before the checks or before the verifier now holds the job: it stays dispatched with its records, no outcome and a hold marker with the amounts. The next drain resumes it from the kept candidate with no planner or producer run. The stale scope_guard test is rewritten to assert the LowDisk hold and a resumed, accepted retry, and the D146 decisions entry passes the backtest. Tests I ran all passed: drain (129), backtest (21), the new binary status test, and the full athena-core suite. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and `cargo test --locked` (1817 tests) also passed. All 16 changed files are on the deliverables list, and no governance file changed. The findings are minor or nit: a misleading test comment; one extra reader call per pass while space stays short (bounded); and an unchecked figure in the decisions entry, whose source records are absent from this snapshot.
